HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The palace steps. Kim Yushin has just dismounted and is laying the torn red Goguryeo flag flat on the stone, both hands, head bowed. King Jinpyung stands two steps up in a thin coat, looking at the flag, not at the crowd. Behind Yushin, his father Seohyun stands, not kneeling, one hand half-raised as if to fix a helmet that is already straight. Pine branches shake at the edge of frame. Crowd bokeh below. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = yushin, SECOND face = jinpyung, THIRD face = seohyeon. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_moon_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels), crown reference (shape only). KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Hwarang years (stage portrait): BEARDLESS, Silla-blue headband with a gold crescent moon, its tails trailing. Colour #2A5FB8. KING JINPYUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #5a86d6. KIM SEOHYUN — Look: Gentle long face, apologetic eyes, a careful mouth; a softer cousin of young Yushin's face, never the same man. Completely clean-shaven and long-haired when young (loose topknot, long strands past the jaw); a thin moustache and short beard from his forties. Now: Grey-templed provincial governor and general; Silla steel lamellar on campaign. Colour #3E8EF0. PLACE Moon Palace (월궁) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
